stories.title: EA is closing BioWare and ending work on the next Mass Effect
paragraphs: BioWare said it is closing after more than three decades and that early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.
The Associated Press placed the move within a wider EA layoff round affecting more than 400 employees. BioWare made Dragon Age and Mass Effect, two of EA's best-known role-playing franchises.

The closure removes a veteran studio from a difficult market for game development and leaves the next Mass Effect canceled. Fan and developer reactions appeared across the saved reporting and sampled community threads.

scoreNotes.general: A consequential studio closure and franchise cancellation with direct confirmation and broad industry impact.
scoreNotes.heat: BioWare is a long-running, prominent RPG studio; the closure and cancellation prompted extensive fan and developer discussion in the saved results.
scoreNotes.time: The announcement and coverage landed within the past few days, outside this edition's exact 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: BioWare's statement confirms the closure and project ending; AP reports the broader EA layoffs. The saved evidence does not explain every affected role or project.

citations.title: Video game developer BioWare shuts down, next 'Mass Effect' canceled amid broader layoffs at EA

stories.title: Inoxtag is bringing a 60-creator Fortnite tournament to Paris Games Week
paragraphs: French creator Inoxtag's Back to OG is scheduled as a Fortnite tournament at the Dome de Paris during Paris Games Week on October 24.

A Paris Games Week preview identifies 60 participating creators. The organizer's page promotes the competition and its prize, but the saved evidence does not establish expected viewership or the final audience size.

The event brings a creator-led competition into a major in-person gaming week, giving it a broader live audience than an ordinary creator stream. Its results and turnout were not yet available in the saved research.

scoreNotes.general: A large creator-run live event with a near-term date and a substantial roster, though audience results are not yet available.
scoreNotes.heat: The preview describes 60 creators and the event is part of a major public gaming convention; no viewership forecast is in the saved evidence.
scoreNotes.time: The event is scheduled for October 24, and a Paris Games Week creator preview was published October 22.
scoreNotes.ethos: The event page and a creator-industry publication support the date and format. Attendance and audience response remain prospective.

nearMisses.title: Steam Next Fest's AI-game backlash continues
nearMisses.reason: Owl already covered the same AI-content and discovery backlash. The saved results show more player complaints and reporting, but no verified Valve response or other clear change since that edition, so this remains a Crumb instead of a repeated main story.

scoreNotes.general: A prominent discussion about discovery on Steam, but the current evidence largely extends the already-covered dispute.
scoreNotes.heat: Multiple sampled discussion threads drew attention, including a post with thousands of votes; these samples do not represent all Steam users.
scoreNotes.time: New discussion appeared during the October festival, which runs through October 26.
scoreNotes.ethos: The complaint trend is supported by reporting and sampled posts. Claims about which games use AI are not independently verified, and no Valve response was found.

paragraphs: PC Gamer reported that October's Steam Next Fest included more than 8,000 demos, roughly twice the number in June; players continued to complain about AI-generated or low-effort entries.

An October 22 r/IndieDev thread added more complaints about games with apparent AI content and disclosure. That thread is a sample of community discussion, not a measure of player opinion across Steam.
The saved results did not establish a Valve policy change or a response to the complaints.
